rationale: Both compile user definitions into closures at definition time, which is the right design. B is better structured. It moves body compilation into a documented compile helper and number detection into parseNumber, which removes the duplicated parse-or-lookup logic that A repeats in two places. B also handles a definition anywhere in a line by scanning for ';', while A only recognises a definition that occupies the whole line. A's helpers popOne and popTwo are misleadingly named: they only peek, and the callers then modify the slice by hand. A's package-level sentinel errors are nicer than B's repeated errors.New strings. B's swap and over also report 'only one value' even when the stack is empty. Overall B's decomposition and generality make it clearer and more robust.
